title: GradRatio-Select: Gradient-Based Layer Selection for Fine-Tuning Model Editing

contributions.purpose: Provide a principled, automatic way to choose which transformer layer to fine-tune for model editing.
contributions.mechanism: Propose GradRatio scoring, a gradient-based metric S(l) = ||g_edit||^2 / ||g_retain||^2 that ranks layer editability by the ratio of edit-to-retain gradient magnitudes.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a metric that selects the layer with the highest score across candidate layers.
contributions.source_quote: We propose GradRatio scoring, a gradient-based metric for evaluating layer editability based on the ratio of edit-to-retain gradient magnitudes.

contributions.purpose: Prevent catastrophic capability loss from editing critical layers.
contributions.mechanism: Introduce an adaptive threshold mechanism that excludes structurally critical early layers from selection.
contributions.evaluation: Described as preventing capability catastrophe (no standalone metric).
contributions.source_quote: We introduce an adaptive threshold mechanism that excludes structurally critical early layers, preventing capability catastrophe.

contributions.purpose: Empirically assess whether gradient-based selection improves over manual heuristics.
contributions.mechanism: Compare GradRatio-Select against manually-tuned layer heuristics on Qwen2.5-7B and LLaMA-3-8B.
contributions.evaluation: Matches heuristics on Qwen2.5-7B (Capability 54.59 vs 54.61) but underperforms on LLaMA-3-8B (5.26pp degradation, 39.52 vs 44.78, driven by math reasoning); provides automation without improvement.
contributions.source_quote: We provide empirical evaluation showing that GradRatio-Select matches heuristic performance on Qwen2.5-7B but underperforms on LLaMA-3-8B, demonstrating that gradient-based selection provides automation without improvement.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Fine-tuning-based editing offers a simpler alternative: directly optimizing a subset of model parameters on the edit examples (Yang et al. 2025b). ... Current practice relies on model-specific heuristics ... determined through expensive layer sweeps (Yang et al. 2025b).
Fine-tuning-based editing (Yang et al. 2025b) updates a subset of parameters W_l at a single layer l to minimize an edit objective while maintaining performance on a retain set.

notes: No-improvement / partially negative result: authors explicitly conclude gradient-based selection 'can automate layer identification but does not improve upon carefully-tuned heuristics' - a tie on Qwen2.5-7B (54.59 vs 54.61) and a 5.26pp degradation on LLaMA-3-8B (39.52 vs 44.78).
